down.types: Down is sold by species, composition and loft. Goose and duck down dominate; mature birds give larger clusters. Fill power, the volume one ounce occupies under a standard test, is the main loft class: duck down commonly tests around 550 to 750, while goose down reaches higher values, and fills above about 800 are mostly mature goose. Composition is stated as a down to feather ratio such as 90/10 or 80/20, meaning percent down cluster and percent feather. In US industry practice a product labeled down needs at least 75 percent down cluster, and species labels such as goose down must be nearly all that species. European EN 12934 uses different thresholds and categories.
down.fabrics: Down fills puffer jackets, vests, sleeping bags, quilts, comforters (duvets) and pillows. It is held in down-proof shells: tightly woven cotton cambric, batiste or sateen in bedding, and calendered or coated nylon or polyester ripstop in outdoor gear. Construction matters as much as fill: sewn-through quilting is light but creates cold spots at seams, while baffle-box walls let down loft fully. Hydrophobic down, treated with a durable water repellent finish, is used in some outdoor products. Blends with polyester fiber or feathers are used in cheaper bedding.
down.quality: Check four label items: species, down to feather ratio, fill power and fill weight. Fill power sets loft per ounce, but warmth depends on fill weight too, so a heavier 650 fill can be warmer than a light 850 fill. Fill power figures from US and European methods are not directly comparable. Quills poking through or a crunchy feel indicate feather content; a musty smell when damp suggests poorly washed down. Look for test reports from recognized labs and welfare certification such as the Responsible Down Standard. Very high fill power at a low price is a red flag. The FTC treats overstated down percentages as deceptive.
pros: Down gives more warmth for its weight than most fiber insulations when dry.
It compresses small and recovers loft many times, suiting packable gear.
Well-cared-for down products can last for decades and down can be recycled.
Down is a by-product of poultry meat production.
cons: Wet down clumps and loses most of its insulation, and dries slowly.
Live plucking and force-feeding for foie gras are welfare risks unless the supply chain is certified.
Species, fill power and down percentage are easy to overstate and hard to check without lab testing.
Washing and drying need care to avoid clumping and odor.
down.impact: Down is mostly a by-product of duck and goose meat production, and how its footprint is allocated is contested. The EU Product Environmental Footprint database gives about 4.15 kg CO2e per kg of virgin down including bird raising, a figure the processor ALLIED Feather + Down cited in 2026 when reporting its own audited processing at about 0.48 kg CO2e per kg. An LCA commissioned by the International Down and Feather Bureau from Long Trail Sustainability reported 85 to 97 percent lower impacts per ton for down than polyester fill; it is industry-funded. Welfare is the main social issue: the Responsible Down Standard, launched in January 2014 by The North Face, Textile Exchange and Control Union, prohibits live plucking and force-feeding.
down.care: Wash down products only when needed, in a large front-loading machine without an agitator, on a gentle cycle at about 30 C or as labeled, with a down-specific detergent; ordinary detergents and fabric softener strip natural oils and reduce loft. Rinse twice to remove residue. Tumble dry on low heat with clean dryer or tennis balls, for several hours, until no clumps remain; damp down left in clumps can mildew and smell. Spot clean shells with mild soap. Store lofted in a large breathable bag, never compressed in a stuff sack. Air comforters in the sun occasionally. The product label governs.
faq: What does 90/10 mean on a down comforter?

It means about 90 percent down cluster and 10 percent feathers by weight. Higher down ratios usually mean lighter, loftier fill. In the US, a product labeled down needs at least 75 percent down cluster, and labels below that must state both down and feather percentages.
Is goose down better than duck down?

Goose down clusters are often larger, so the highest fill powers are usually goose. But a mature duck down can outperform immature goose down. Compare stated fill power and fill weight rather than species alone.
What fill power do I need?

About 550 to 650 suits everyday bedding and casual jackets, 700 to 800 gives lighter, more packable warmth, and 800 or more is used where weight matters most, such as ultralight sleeping bags. Fill weight determines total warmth.
How do I know down was not live-plucked?

Look for a recognized welfare certification such as the Responsible Down Standard, which prohibits live plucking and force-feeding and tracks certified down through the supply chain. Live plucking cannot be detected by testing the finished fill.
Can a down duvet be washed at home?

Often yes, if it fits loosely in a large front-loading machine. Use a down detergent, a gentle cycle and a long, low-heat tumble dry with dryer balls. Oversized comforters are better sent to a professional cleaner.
notable: US industry labeling requires at least 75 percent down cluster for a product called down, while EN 12934 in Europe uses a lower threshold defined differently.
The Responsible Down Standard began as a The North Face initiative and was handed to Textile Exchange, launching in January 2014.
One down processor reported in 2026 an audited footprint of about 0.48 kg CO2e per kg of down, far below the EU database value of about 4.15.
